key_insight: EATS improves medical agents’ tool selection by retrieving relevant past tool-use experiences rather than relying only on tool descriptions.
clinical_relevance: More effective use of specialized tools could support medical image question answering and report generation, but clinical benefit remains unproven.
method: Store queries, tool choices, arguments, and self-evaluated feedback in an experience memory.
Retrieve relevant experiences to guide tool selection for new queries.
Expand memory through test-time interactions without ground-truth supervision.
evidence_signal: Across four public datasets—ChestAgentBench, CheXbench, MIMIC-CXR, and SLAKE-VQA—and three multimodal LLMs, the abstract reports consistent gains in tool selection and downstream task performance, without numerical effect sizes.
watch_item: Self-evaluated feedback may preserve errors in memory; reliability under clinical distribution shifts needs validation.
paper_title: EATS: Scaling Tool-Use Experience for Medical Reasoning Agents
